extracted.intended_audience: county government officials, planners and public-participation practitioners implementing the Kenya Affordable Housing Programme
extracted.subtask_short: public participation in county housing planning
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal requirements for designing and conducting public participation in county-level affordable housing planning and related decision-making under Kenyan law. Covers constitutional bases, county duties, budgetary participation, required information disclosure, institutional mechanisms and accommodations for disadvantaged groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional basis for public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation is an express constitutional power and national value; all sovereign power belongs to the people who may exercise it directly or through representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Constitution of Kenya 2010 (Articles 1(2), 10(2), 174(1)). Establishes that citizens have the right to have their opinion heard on matters of national importance and to be involved in democratic and governance processes at national and county levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation in environmental management
rubrics_metrics.description: The State shall encourage public participation in the management, protection and conservation of the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Article 69(d) — participation requirement applies to environmental decision-making and related planning processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary and county assembly duty to facilitate public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament and County Assemblies must facilitate public participation and involvement in their legislative and other business and committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Articles 118(b) and 196(b) — implies legislative processes must include mechanisms for public input and involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and accountability including participation in financial matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation is required as part of openness and accountability in all aspects of public finance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Article 201(a) — applies to budgetary and financial decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counties must establish public communication and information-access mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: County governments are required to establish mechanisms to facilitate public communication and access to information with the widest public outreach using media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites County Government Act Sections 94 and 95 — emphasizes proactive information dissemination and use of media for outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional framework for civic education
rubrics_metrics.description: County governments should create an institutional framework to provide civic education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites County Government Act Sections 100 and 101 — supports informed participation by educating citizens about processes and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor and county executive responsibility to promote citizen participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor and county executive committee members must promote and facilitate citizen participation in policy, plan development and service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Section 30(3)(g) and Section 46(2)(g) of the County Governments Act — places affirmative duty on executive-level officials to enable participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local referendum mechanism for county issues
rubrics_metrics.description: A county government may conduct a local referendum on local issues, county laws, petitions, planning and investment decisions when a petition is signed by at least 25% of registered voters where the referendum is to take place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites County Governments Act Section 70 — specifies threshold (25%) and subjects appropriate for local referenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: County assembly members’ role to consult electorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the County Assembly shall maintain close contact with the electorate and consult them on issues before or under discussion, providing a linkage between the assembly and the electorate on public service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites County Governments Act Section 9 — expects active engagement by representatives to foster participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of non-state actors in planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-state actors shall be incorporated in planning processes by all authorities to promote public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites County Governments Act Section 104(4) — explicitly requires the inclusion of NGOs, community groups, private sector or other non-state stakeholders in planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory public participation in county planning with clear information disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation in county planning processes shall be mandatory and facilitated through mechanisms provided in the Act, with provision to the public of clear and unambiguous information on any matter under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites County Governments Act Section 115 — requires disclosure of clear strategic environmental assessments, clear environmental impact assessment reports, expected development outcomes, development options and their cost implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counties must enact local laws/guidelines meeting minimum national participation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each county shall develop laws and regulations giving effect to effective citizen participation in development planning and performance management, which must adhere to minimum national requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites County Governments Act Section 115 (further provision) — local legal frameworks must implement national baseline standards for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: County structures, mechanisms and guidelines for citizen participation in public finance
rubrics_metrics.description: County governments are to establish structures, mechanisms and guidelines specifically for citizen participation in public finance and budgeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Public Finance Management Act Section 207 and related sections (e.g., Sections 10, 35, 125, 175(9)) — includes requirement that Parliamentary Budget Office and budget officials observe/ensure public participation at national and county budget stages; urban authorities may publish participation guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory elements for participatory governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations under the Public Finance Management Act may provide for detailed participatory governance elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Sections 205 and 207 — lists possible regulatory elements: structures for participation; mechanisms, processes and procedures for participation; receipt, processing and consideration of petitions and complaints; notification and public comment procedures; public meetings and hearings; accommodations for special needs; matters encouraged for community participation; rights and duties of community members; and any other matter that enhances community participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide for receipt and consideration of petitions and complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations should include processes for receipt, processing and consideration of petitions and complaints lodged by community members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated under Sections 205/207 — implies clear administrative pathways and timelines for handling civic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and public comment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be formal notification mechanisms and opportunities for public comment on matters under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among regulatory provisions in Sections 205/207 — covers how the public is informed and how comments are solicited, received and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public meetings and hearings as part of participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public meetings and hearings should be used as mechanisms for community participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in Sections 205/207 — includes open sessions where stakeholders can express views and officials can record input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodations for persons with special needs and disadvantaged groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation processes must account for the special needs of people who cannot read or write, people with disabilities, women and other disadvantaged groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically enumerated in Sections 205/207 — requires accessible formats, outreach and facilitation to ensure inclusive participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define matters for which community participation is encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations should identify the types of matters for which community participation is explicitly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the list in Sections 205/207 — guidance to specify subject-matters (e.g., planning, investment decisions) where participation is required or prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify rights and duties of community members in participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation frameworks should set out the rights and duties of community members engaging in public participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in Sections 205/207 — helps manage expectations and responsibilities of participants and authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multiple avenues for urban/resident participation (fora, pacts, MOUs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Urban Areas and Cities Act requires participation by residents and provides for avenues such as citizen’s fora, development pacts and MOUs between public service providers and representatives of citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Urban Areas and Cities Act Second Schedule — encourages formalized, institutionalized participation arrangements in cities and urban areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework law for coordinated and effective public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Public Participation Bill should provide a framework for effective and coordinated public participation across public processes, giving effect to constitutional principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Public Participation Bill 2016 — frames participation as required across policy-making, legislative process and decision-making; emphasizes coordination and mechanisms to operationalize constitutional principles (Articles cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure participation in transition to devolved government
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies managing the transition to devolved government must be accountable to the people and ensure their participation in the transition process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Transition to Devolved Government Act Section 14 — applicable to authorities like the Transition Authority during devolution processes.
